ican.text: I can transform a point or shape using a matrix and translation vector.
I can identify and construct matrices for standard reflections, stretches, enlargements and rotations about the origin.
I can compose transformations in the correct order and combine their translations.
I can use the determinant to find an area scale factor and interpret a zero or negative determinant.
I can apply an iterative rule and explain how repeated contractions can generate a fractal.

ku.text: Use column vectors throughout: $\mathbf{x}=\binom{x}{y}$. An affine transformation has the form $\mathbf{x}\mapsto A\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{b}$, where $A$ is $2\times2$ and $\mathbf{b}$ is a translation column. Apply $A$ first, then add $\mathbf{b}$.

The columns of $A$ are the images of the basis vectors $\binom10$ and $\binom01$ under the linear part. A translation moves the origin, so subtract the image of the origin when recovering these columns from an affine transformation.
Reflection in the $x$-axis has matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$; reflection in the $y$-axis has $\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$; reflection in $y=x$ swaps the coordinates.

A horizontal stretch by factor $a$ and vertical stretch by factor $b$ has matrix $\begin{pmatrix}a&0\\0&b\end{pmatrix}$. Equal factors give an enlargement about the origin; a negative factor reverses the corresponding coordinate.

An anticlockwise rotation through $\theta$ about the origin has matrix $\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}$. A clockwise rotation through a positive angle uses $-\theta$. Check the angle mode and the image of $(1,0)$.

If $T_1(\mathbf{x})=A\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{b}$ is followed by $T_2(\mathbf{x})=B\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{c}$, then $T_2(T_1(\mathbf{x}))=BA\mathbf{x}+B\mathbf{b}+\mathbf{c}$. The rightmost matrix acts first; the earlier translation is transformed too.

For any planar region with finite area, an affine map scales area by $|\det A|$. A negative determinant reverses orientation, a positive determinant preserves it when nonzero, and determinant zero collapses area to zero. Translation does not affect area.

An inverse transformation exists exactly when $\det A\ne0$. Solve $\mathbf{y}=A\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{b}$ as $\mathbf{x}=A^{-1}(\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{b})$; subtract the translation before applying the inverse matrix.

An iterative rule repeatedly uses the preceding output, for example $\mathbf{x}_{n+1}=A\mathbf{x}_n+\mathbf{b}$. A fractal construction can instead repeatedly apply several contractions to a set and take their union. The rule, starting set and iteration count determine the result.

For example, applying three half-scale copies to a triangle at its three corners produces three smaller triangles at each stage. After $n$ stages there are $3^n$ copies, each with area factor $(1/4)^n$; the total area factor is $(3/4)^n$ when their interiors do not overlap.

misc.better: With column vectors, $A$ acts first and $B$ acts on its result.

misc.weak: A translation can be represented by a $2\times2$ matrix acting alone on every point.
misc.better: A linear matrix fixes the origin. A nonzero translation requires an added vector in the given affine form.

misc.weak: A negative determinant means the image has negative area.
misc.better: Area is multiplied by $|\det A|$. The sign describes orientation for a non-singular map.
The second matrix also acts on the first translation: $BA\mathbf{x}+B\mathbf{b}+\mathbf{c}$.

misc.weak: A matrix with determinant zero has an inverse.
misc.better: A zero determinant means the map collapses area and is singular; it has no inverse matrix.
It maps $(1,0)$ to $(0,1)$ in standard Cartesian axes.

terms.text: The point or shape resulting from the transformation.
Applying transformations in sequence; the order affects the result.
The displacement added to the output of the matrix part.
A scalar associated with a square matrix. Its absolute value gives the planar area scale factor.
Repeated application of a rule, using an earlier result as the next input.
A transformation that reduces distances by a factor less than one; repeated contractions can be used in fractal constructions.

formula.text: Affine form: $\mathbf{x}\mapsto A\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{b}$ for column vectors.
If $A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$, then $\det A=ad-bc$ and image area is $|\det A|$ times original area.

worked.prompt: A transformation sends $\binom{x}{y}$ to $A\binom{x}{y}+\binom31$, where $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&-2\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$. Triangle $PQR$ has vertices $P=(0,0)$, $Q=(2,0)$ and $R=(0,1)$.

parts.label: a
parts.q: Find the image of each vertex and the area of the image.
parts.a: The coordinate rule is $(x,y)\mapsto(3-2y,x+1)$. Hence $P\mapsto(3,1)$, $Q\mapsto(3,3)$ and $R\mapsto(1,1)$. The original area is $\frac12(2)(1)=1$ square unit. Since $\det A=2$, image area is $2$ square units. The image is also a right triangle with legs of length $2$.

parts.label: b
parts.q: Describe the linear part as a composition of a rotation and a stretch. State the order.
parts.a: First rotate $90^\circ$ anticlockwise using $R=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, then stretch horizontally by factor $2$ using $S=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$. Indeed $SR=A$. The translation $(3,1)$ is applied after those linear steps.

parts.label: c
parts.q: Starting from $(1,2)$, find the next three points when the whole affine transformation is iterated.
parts.a: Use $(x,y)\mapsto(3-2y,x+1)$ repeatedly: $(1,2)\mapsto(-1,2)\mapsto(-1,0)\mapsto(3,0)$. The translation is included at every iteration.

parts.label: d
parts.q: Find the fixed point of the transformation.
parts.a: Set $x=3-2y$ and $y=x+1$. Substitution gives $x=3-2(x+1)$, so $3x=1$ and $x=1/3$. Then $y=4/3$. The fixed point is $(1/3,4/3)$.

parts.label: e
parts.q: A separate construction begins with a triangle of area $12$ square units. At each stage it is replaced by three half-scale copies with non-overlapping interiors. Find the total area after two stages.
parts.a: Each half-scale copy has area factor $(1/2)^2=1/4$, so the total area factor per stage is $3/4$. After two stages, the area is $12(3/4)^2=6.75$ square units.

kq.q: Why is the order of matrix multiplication important?
kq.model: Each transformation acts on the result of the preceding one, and matrix multiplication is generally not commutative. The rightmost matrix acts first on a column vector.

kq.q: Why does translation not change area?
kq.model: Every point moves by the same displacement. The shape and its lengths and area are unchanged.

kq.q: Why is the area factor an absolute value?
kq.model: A negative determinant indicates an orientation reversal, but geometric area is nonnegative. The magnitude gives the scale factor.

kq.q: Why does half-scale copying multiply area by one quarter per copy?
kq.model: Both independent length dimensions are halved, so the area scale is $(1/2)(1/2)=1/4$.
